findings.title: "so they are unaffected" is false for v0.9 components whose schema omits accessibility
findings.where: commit message, paragraph 2, last sentence ("v0.9 components declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon, whose v0.9 schema has no `hidden`, so they are unaffected.")
findings.evidence: _withAccessibility (generic_binder.dart L606-L626) checks only whether the root shape has an `accessibility` key. It does not check the protocol version. The message's own first sentence says the binder injects for "every component whose schema does not declare `accessibility`". The v0.9 basic catalog components do allOf v0.9 ComponentCommon, so they are unaffected, and my probe confirmed it: v0.9 BasicCatalog Text with `accessibility: {hidden: {path: /h}}` still gives `hidden: {path: /h}`. But a v0.9 catalog component whose schema leaves out ComponentCommon (Schema.object(properties: {'text': dynamicString}), protocolVersion v0_9, surface v0.9) does change. Before the commit it gives `hidden: {path: /h}`. At d7e5f437 it gives `hidden: WritableBinding(true, path: /h)`. Probe run in a throwaway worktree, once at d7e5f437 and once with the added line reverted.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "v0.9 components that declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon, as every basic catalog component does, keep the v0.9 schema, which has no `hidden`, so they are unaffected. A v0.9 component whose schema omits `accessibility` gets the injected behavior and now resolves `hidden` too, as it already resolved `label` and `description`."

votes.reasoning:
I read the code and the spec and ran no probe. At d7e5f437, `_withAccessibility` (generic_binder.dart L606-L626, called for every component schema at L116) checks only `root.type == object`, a non-null shape, and whether `accessibility` is already in the shape. It never looks at the protocol or catalog version. So the commit adds `hidden` to the injected envelope for every component, v0.9 included, whose root schema has no `accessibility` property.

The message's closing sentence states a universal: "v0.9 components declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon ... so they are unaffected." That holds for the v0.9 basic catalog, whose components allOf ComponentCommon. In specification/v0_9/json/common_types.json, ComponentCommon's AccessibilityAttributes has only `label` and `description`. But nothing in specification/v0_9/docs requires a catalog component to include ComponentCommon (grep found no mention), so a custom v0.9 catalog can leave it out. Such a component already got the injected `label` and `description` before this commit. After it, an `accessibility.hidden` in its payload resolves to a binding instead of the raw `{"@path": ...}` map, which is exactly what the reviewer's probe showed.

The claim is therefore overbroad and breaks the author's rule that every factual claim is true at the commit. The practical impact is tiny: v0.9 defines no `hidden`, so only an off-spec v0.9 payload sees the change, and that change is benign. That makes it should-fix rather than blocker. The proposed fix is accurate but wordier than it needs to be.
votes.corrected_fix: Replace the last sentence of paragraph 2 with: "v0.9 basic catalog components declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon, whose v0.9 schema has no `hidden`, so they are unaffected. A v0.9 component whose schema leaves out `accessibility` gets the injected `hidden` along with `label` and `description`, which changes nothing for a valid v0.9 payload, since v0.9 defines no `hidden`."

votes.reasoning:
I read d7e5f437, the binder at that commit, and the v0.9 schemas. I did not run a probe myself because the code settles the question.

- **The injection ignores protocol version.** `_withAccessibility` (generic_binder.dart L606-L626, called at L116 on every scraped schema) checks only whether the root shape has an `accessibility` key. Any object-shaped component schema without that key, v0.9 included, now gets `hidden` as `Behavior.dynamic` next to `label` and `description`.
- **The v0.9 spec doesn't require ComponentCommon.** `grep -rln ComponentCommon specification/v0_9` finds only `common_types.json` and the basic and minimal catalogs. No v0.9 doc or `server_to_client.json` requires a component to include it. So the message's general claim "v0.9 components declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon" holds only for those catalogs.
- **The effect is real.** A v0.9 custom component whose schema omits `accessibility` and receives `accessibility.hidden` gets a resolved binding instead of the raw `{path: ...}` map. That matches the reviewer's before/after probe. The sentence "so they are unaffected" is therefore false at this commit.

**Why should-fix and not blocker:** `hidden` doesn't exist in v0.9 `AccessibilityAttributes`, so only off-spec v0.9 input is affected. The change is harmless and matches how `label` and `description` already behave. The message still overstates its scope, and a porter could rely on that sentence, so it needs correcting.

**Proposed fix:** it is accurate but wordier than needed. A tighter version is below.
votes.corrected_fix: Replace the last sentence of paragraph 2 with: "v0.9 components that declare `accessibility` through ComponentCommon, as the basic catalog's do, keep the v0.9 schema, which has no `hidden`, so they are unaffected. A v0.9 component whose schema omits `accessibility` gets the injected behavior, so a `hidden` sent to it now resolves too, as `label` and `description` already did."

findings.title: A literal or absent hidden also changes shape in node.props, and the message only implies it
findings.where: commit message, paragraph 2 ("on a v1.0 component it reaches `node.props` as a binding to its value"), and the CHANGELOG entry
findings.evidence: Probe on the v1.0 basic catalog Text. Before the commit, `{hidden: true}` reached props as `hidden: true` (a bare bool). At d7e5f437 it reaches them as `ResolvedBinding(true)`. Before the commit, `{label: 'L'}` had no `hidden` key. At d7e5f437 it has `hidden: ResolvedBinding(null)`, and the edited test asserts this with `_expectReadOnlyNull(accessibility['hidden'])`. A consumer that read a literal `hidden` as a bool would now see a binding. No reader exists at this commit: NodeView reads only label and description, and origin/feat/flutter-adapter-v1_0 has no `hidden` reader. So nothing breaks, but a porter has to infer this from "a binding to its value".
findings.fix: Add after that sentence: "A literal `hidden` now arrives as a read-only binding rather than a bare bool, and an omitted one as a null binding, as `label` and `description` already do."

votes.reasoning:
The finding's facts are right, but the message already states them. In the diff, `_withAccessibility` in generic_binder.dart changes `hidden` from absent in the envelope shape, which made it Behavior.static and passed the raw value through, to `BehaviorNode(Behavior.dynamic)`, the same as `label` and `description`. So a literal `hidden: true` was a bare bool before and is a ResolvedBinding(true) now. An omitted `hidden` next to a given `label` now arrives as a read-only null binding, and the edited test confirms this with `_expectReadOnlyNull(accessibility['hidden'])`. I verified this by reading the diff and the parent's binder. I did not run a probe, because the diff and the test settle the behaviour.

The message does not leave this to inference. It says "`hidden` now resolves like `label` and `description`: on a v1.0 component it reaches `node.props` as a binding to its value, and a bound `hidden` follows the data." "It" is any `hidden`, literal or bound. The bound case gets its own clause, so the first clause clearly covers the literal case, and "a binding to its value" is exactly ResolvedBinding(true). "Resolves like `label` and `description`" also covers the omitted case. Those properties already arrive as null read-only bindings when omitted, and the existing test asserts that for `description` on the line right above the new assertion. The CHANGELOG says the same: "so it reaches `node.props` as a binding to its value".

So the claim that the message "only implies it" does not hold, and every claim in the message is true at this commit. The proposed sentence would only restate what the message already says. As the finding itself notes, nothing at this commit or on the other branch reads `hidden`, so no porter is misled. This is not a problem under the author's rules.

I read the commit, its message and the binder hunk at d7e5f437 and its parent. I did not run a probe. The reviewer's description of the behaviour matches the code. Adding `'hidden': BehaviorNode(Behavior.dynamic)` to the `_withAccessibility` shape means a literal `hidden` now becomes a ResolvedBinding, and an omitted one becomes a read-only null binding, as `label` and `description` already do. The edited test asserts the null case with `_expectReadOnlyNull(accessibility['hidden'])`.

The message already says this, though. Paragraph 1 says the binder "left it static" before the commit. Paragraph 2 says "`hidden` now resolves like `label` and `description`: on a v1.0 component it reaches `node.props` as a binding to its value". That sentence names the new shape for every `hidden` on a v1.0 component, literal ones included. Read against "static" in paragraph 1, the change from the written value to a binding is explicit, not just implied.

findings.title: A poster that fails to load hides the ready video's first frame, and the message gives no reason for it

findings.evidence: Message: "A poster that fails to load shows the empty frame." That is true, but it stays true after the video is ready. `hasPoster` only checks the URL scheme, so with a broken http poster, `ready && !hasPoster` is false and the frame stays blank until the user presses play. With no poster at all, the same ready video shows its first frame (`VideoPlayer`). The message holds up HTML `<video poster>` as the model, and HTML shows the first frame of the video when there is no poster frame, including when the poster image fails to load. Probe at 6a244423 (ImageServer with no image, so the poster returns 404, then `platform.initialize(0, size: 1000x1000)`): before ready, VideoPlayer=0 and one ColoredBox in the frame. After ready, still VideoPlayer=0, one ColoredBox, ratio 1.0. The message states the result but not why a broken poster should hide the video when having no poster does not, which is the obvious alternative.
findings.fix: Either fall back to the video once it is ready, with `errorBuilder: (context, error, stackTrace) => ready ? VideoPlayer(controller!) : blank` and the message sentence "A poster that fails to load shows the empty frame until the video is ready, then the video frame, as with no poster." - **The condition.** `hasPoster` is `!failed && (poster.startsWith('http://') || poster.startsWith('https://'))`. It looks only at the URL's scheme, never at whether the image loaded. So with a broken http(s) poster, `started || (ready && !hasPoster)` stays false after the video is ready. The Image.network stays in the tree, and its `errorBuilder` keeps returning `blank` (the surfaceContainerHighest ColoredBox, with no icon because `failed` is false). The VideoPlayer appears only after play (`_played`) or once the position moves past zero.
- **No poster at all.** `hasPoster` is false, so a ready video shows `VideoPlayer(controller!)` right away. A broken poster is therefore treated worse than having no poster.
- **HTML differs.** The message names `<video poster>` as its model, though only for the pause rule. In the HTML spec, a poster image that fails to fetch means "there is no poster frame". A paused video at its first frame with no poster frame shows the first frame of the video. So HTML falls back to the video, and this commit does not.
- **The message.** "A poster that fails to load shows the empty frame." is literally true. But it does not say this lasts after the video is ready, and it gives no reason for departing from both the no-poster path and HTML. The brief requires a reason wherever a choice differs from the obvious alternative.

findings.title: The message does not say why the map rule is looser than the spec's and commit 7f5e2045's shape
findings.evidence: Spec rule 1 coerces "a `ValidationResult` object (an object with a boolean `valid` property)". `ValidationResult.validityOf` accepts any map that contains a `valid` key: `final Map<Object?, Object?> map when map.containsKey('valid') => map['valid'] == true`. So `{"valid": "yes"}` reads as false here instead of null. In the same series, 7f5e2045 reads only "a map of the protocol's ValidationResult shape (a boolean `valid` with nothing beside it but `code`, `message` and `severity`)". The message does give one reason, "the rule a2ui_core's `and`, `or` and `not` use", and the description "or a map with a `valid` key" is accurate. But a porter comparing the two commits sees two rules and no word on why this one follows validityOf instead of the stricter check.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to paragraph 2, for example: "It takes validityOf's rule, under which any map with a `valid` key counts, rather than the stricter shape the argument check uses, so that a property reads a value the way `and`, `or` and `not` read it as an operand."

votes.reasoning:
The facts in the finding are correct, but the message already gives the reason it asks for. At a86dd818, `asBoolean` falls through to `ValidationResult.validityOf` (dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/core/validation_result.dart:82-87). That function treats any map with a `valid` key as `map['valid'] == true`, so `{"valid": "yes"}` reads as false. 7f5e2045 does use a stricter shape for the argument-schema check.

Paragraph 2 describes the looser rule accurately ("a ValidationResult, or a map with a `valid` key") and names where it comes from: "through `ValidationResult.validityOf`, the rule a2ui_core's `and`, `or` and `not` use". Saying the property matches the logic functions is the reason for the choice. The proposed extra sentence only says that again in more words.

The two rules also serve different checks, and 7f5e2045's own message explains its stricter shape. That commit gates a schema check over arbitrary function arguments, so a map that merely has a `valid` key next to other data must not be rewritten. That message also says the functions themselves still read operands through `validityOf`. So a porter reading both commits already sees that `validityOf` is the operand-reading rule and the strict shape is only for the argument check. a86dd818 reads a value as an operand-like boolean, which is exactly where 7f5e2045 says `validityOf` applies.

A DynamicBoolean property that holds a non-result map is off-schema anyway, so the looser match costs nothing a reader needs to be warned about. The other claims check out: the CHANGELOG line, "Any other value that is not a `bool` still reads as null" (true for anything that is not a map with `valid`), and the v0.9 note. By the author's rules, nothing is missing.

I read the a86dd818 message and diff, `ValidationResult.validityOf` in dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/core/validation_result.dart (L82-87), the 7f5e2045 message, and spec section "DynamicBoolean and CheckRule Coercion" (a2ui_protocol.md L1115-1126). The facts in the finding are right. validityOf accepts any map with a `valid` key and returns `map['valid'] == true`. 7f5e2045's argument check uses a stricter shape. But the claim that the message gives no reason does not hold. Paragraph 2 names the rule ("a ValidationResult, or a map with a `valid` key") and gives the reason for it ("through `ValidationResult.validityOf`, the rule a2ui_core's `and`, `or` and `not` use"). That reason is consistency with how operands are read in a boolean position. The proposed sentence says the same thing in more words, so it adds no information.

A porter comparing the two commits would not see a contradiction either. 7f5e2045's own paragraph 3 says that `and`, `or` and `not` read their operands through `ValidationResult.validityOf`, and that its stricter shape applies only to the schema check. That check runs on every argument at any depth, including positions that are not boolean, so it has to be strict. `asBoolean` runs only on a property already in a boolean position, which is why the looser read is safe there. Read together, the two messages already account for the difference.

The edge case the finding gives, `{"valid": "yes"}`, is off-spec input: the spec defines a ValidationResult as "an object with a boolean `valid` property". Neither false nor null is required for it, and the author's rules do not require a message to explain a choice by contrasting it with a separate check in another commit. No wrong claim, no portability problem, and the reason is present.

findings.title: Live-region limit is wrong for TextField (and the README's 'not to a control's' is wrong for TextField and Slider)
findings.where: Message, first 'Known limits' bullet; dart/a2ui_flutter/README.md new sentence after '## Summary'
findings.evidence: Message: "When the changing text sits in a control's own semantics node, as with a Button, CheckBox or TextField, nothing is announced." README: "announces changes to its own text, such as a Text's, not to a control's." Probe at a465dc4a (throwaway worktree, flutter test with a semantics dump), v1.0 surface with live 'polite' on a TextField, CheckBox and Slider, each label bound to /l. The TextField has no separate node: the live flag merges onto the text field's own node (flags: isTextField, ..., isLiveRegion, label "One"). Setting /l to 'Two' changed that node's label to "Two", and the Android bridge sends the announcement on exactly that condition (AccessibilityBridge.java: `object.hasFlag(Flag.IS_LIVE_REGION) && object.didChangeLabel()`). Web's LiveRegion behaviour also announces on a label change. Only the TextField's value ("aaa"->"bbb") goes unannounced, because live regions announce the label, not the value. The Slider's live node carries the label "One\n3" (the label plus the displayed value), so changes to the Slider's label and displayed value are announced too. The claim holds for Button (live node #5 has no label, and the child button node's label went one->two) and for CheckBox (its label sits in a merge-boundary child). The message contradicts itself as well: its second bullet says that on a TextField the explicit label "is joined to the widget's own label", which is the same merge.
findings.fix: Message: "A live region announces changes to its own label. A Button's child text and a CheckBox's label sit in the control's own semantics node below the region, so changes to them are not announced. A TextField's region is the field's own node, so a change of its label is announced but a change of its value is not." README: "... is a live region, which announces changes to its own label, such as a Text's text or a TextField's label, but not to a Button's child text, a CheckBox's label or a TextField's value."

votes.reasoning:
I ran a probe at a465dc4a in a throwaway worktree, since removed. It rendered a v1.0 surface with live 'polite' on a TextField, a CheckBox, a Slider and a Button whose child Text is bound to /l. I printed debugDumpSemanticsTree, set /l from 'One' to 'Two' and /v from 'aaa' to 'bbb', then printed the tree again.

- **TextField:** NodeView's Semantics(container: true, liveRegion: true) has no node of its own. The flag lands on the text field's node (#5: isTextField, ..., isLiveRegion). That node's label went from "One" to "Two" and its value from "aaa" to "bbb". Live regions announce label changes, so the TextField's label change is announced and only the value change is not. The message lists TextField among controls where "nothing is announced", which is wrong.
- **Slider:** the live node #10 has its own label, "One\n3" before and "Two\n3" after. So the README's "not to a control's" is also wrong for a Slider's label and displayed value.
- **Button:** live node #12 has no label, and the change is on child button node #13. The claim holds.
- **CheckBox:** live node #6 has no label, and the label sits under merge-boundary node #7. The claim holds.

The message also contradicts itself. Its second bullet says that on a TextField the explicit label "is joined to the widget's own label", which is the same merge onto one node. The brief counts a wrong factual claim as a blocker, and this one is also in the user-facing README. I did not re-read the Android bridge source myself, but the label-on-live-region rule is the standard Flutter behaviour, and the tree dump settles the node structure on its own.

The proposed fix is accurate. It could optionally name the Slider in the README, since its region's label carries both the label and the displayed value.
votes.corrected_fix: Message, first Known limits bullet: "A live region announces changes to its own label. A Button's child text and a CheckBox's label sit in the control's own semantics node below the region, so changes to them are not announced. A TextField's region is the field's own node, so a change to its label is announced but a change to its value is not." README, replacing "which announces changes to its own text, such as a Text's, not to a control's.": "which announces changes to its own label, such as a Text's text, a TextField's label or a Slider's label, but not a Button's child text, a CheckBox's label or a TextField's value."

votes.reasoning:
I ran a probe in a throwaway worktree at a465dc4a (since removed). It renders a v1.0 surface with accessibility.live 'polite' on a TextField, CheckBox, Slider and Button, binds the label (for the Button, its child Text) to /l, then sets /l from 'One' to 'Two' and /v from 'aaa' to 'bbb'. For each run I listed every semantics node that has isLiveRegion set.

- TextField: before, #5 label=One value=aaa isTextField=true. After, #5 label=Two value=bbb. The live flag merges onto the field's own node, so the label change reaches the live node. The value change does too, but that is not the label.
- Slider: label goes from "One\n3" to "Two\n3" on the live node. Changes to the label, and to the displayed value that the label includes, are on the live node.
- CheckBox: the live node has an empty label before and after. The label sits in the MergeSemantics child.
- Button: the live node has an empty label before and after. The text is in the child button node.

I read the Flutter engine source the repo builds with. The Android AccessibilityBridge.java (line 1705) sends a content-change event when `object.hasFlag(Flag.IS_LIVE_REGION) && object.didChangeLabel()`. The web LiveRegion.update() announces semanticsObject.label whenever the label changes.

So on Android and web, changes to a TextField's label and to a Slider's label or displayed value are announced. The message's sentence "When the changing text sits in a control's own semantics node, as with a Button, CheckBox or TextField, nothing is announced" is wrong for TextField. A typed value is not announced, but its label is. The README's "announces changes to its own text, such as a Text's, not to a control's" is wrong for TextField and Slider. The message also contradicts itself: its second bullet says a TextField's explicit label "is joined to the widget's own label", which is the same merge.

Under the brief's rubric, a factual claim that is false at the commit is a blocker, and this one ships in the user-facing README. The proposed fix is right for the message. Its README wording leaves out the Slider, whose label and displayed value are announced too.

findings.title: The forced container for a live node and the choice of liveRegion over an assertive announcement are not explained
findings.where: Message first bullet; node_view.dart `container: label != null || description != null || live != null`
findings.evidence: The diff makes a component with only `live` a semantics container, which it was not before. Without that, the flag would merge into the nearest ancestor boundary. Flutter has `Assertiveness.assertive` for `SemanticsService` announcements (semantics_event.dart), which is the obvious alternative for `assertive`, and the message gives no reason for not using it.

Flutter merges flags on a non-container Semantics into the nearest ancestor boundary. In the test, three live and non-live Text siblings sit in a Column, and without the container they would merge into one node, so the change is needed rather than a hidden choice. An extra sentence about it would only restate the code.

Assertive half, confirmed: the message explains why both levels collapse to one ("Flutter's `Semantics.liveRegion` is a single flag with no assertive level, so both announce politely"). It never says why `assertive` does not use Flutter's real assertive path. That path is `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(view, msg, dir, assertiveness: Assertiveness.assertive)`, checked in the repo's Flutter SDK (semantics_event.dart:18, semantics_service.dart:81). The older `announce` it replaces has been deprecated since 3.35. The brief asks for a reason wherever a choice differs from the obvious alternative, and a porter could reasonably ask about this one. After "so both announce politely." add one sentence, worded so it does not invent a reason the author did not have, for example: "An assertive announcement through `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement` would need NodeView to detect each change to the text itself, so `assertive` stays on the region flag the blueprint's Semantics mapping gives."

I read commit a465dc4a and the Flutter SDK sources on PATH (semantics_event.dart, semantics_service.dart, semantics.dart). The finding has two parts, and neither is a real gap.

1. Why `assertive` is not an assertive announcement. The message already gives the reason: "Flutter's `Semantics.liveRegion` is a single flag with no assertive level, so both announce politely." That is true. `liveRegion` is a `bool?` that controls `SemanticsFlag.isLiveRegion`. `Assertiveness` exists only as a parameter of the imperative `SemanticsService.announce` / `sendAnnouncement` (semantics_service.dart L56-L86), which sends a one-off `AnnounceSemanticsEvent`. `accessibility.live` is a declarative attribute on a component, so the obvious match is the declarative live-region flag, not an imperative announce call. The imperative path would need NodeView to watch for text changes and send messages itself. The brief asks for a reason where a choice departs from the obvious alternative. Here the obvious alternative is the one taken, and its limit is stated. The proposed extra sentence also guesses at a reason ("or whatever the actual reason is"), which would add an unverified claim.

2. The forced `container` for a live node. This is not a choice with a real alternative. A non-container Semantics annotation is merged into the nearest ancestor semantics boundary. Without `container`, the live flag would land on an ancestor's node, such as the enclosing Column's, which would simply be wrong. The pre-existing code already forced `container` for `label`/`description`, for the same reason. The message says the attributes go on "a Semantics node around each resolved component" and that `polite`/`assertive` "make that node a live region", which describes the diff accurately. It also says that `off`, or no `live`, "sets no flag at all, which leaves the semantics of every other component as it was", which tells the reader that a live component's semantics do change. The container flag is a mechanical requirement for "that node" to exist, not a design decision a porter needs explained. At most it is optional polish, not a defect by the author's rules.

The claims the finding touches are accurate at this commit, and no reason is missing.

I read the commit (a465dc4a) and Flutter's semantics_service.dart and semantics_event.dart in the SDK on PATH (~/Documents/GitHub/flutter). I ran no probe because the finding is about what the message says, not about behaviour.

1. The assertive choice is already explained. The message says: "Flutter's `Semantics.liveRegion` is a single flag with no assertive level, so both announce politely." That is the reason for the mapping. SemanticsService is not a real alternative that needs its own justification. Its doc, shared by `announce` and `sendAnnouncement`, says the assertiveness level "is only supported by the web engine and has no effect on other platforms". It also says Android has deprecated announcement events and recommends using `Semantics` instead to trigger announcements. So `Assertiveness.assertive` would help on web only, and only at the cost of hand-rolled change detection. The rule "give the reason where it differs from the obvious alternative" is satisfied, because liveRegion is the idiomatic Flutter mechanism and the message names its limit. The proposed sentence ("would need the adapter to detect each change itself") is also not the main reason. The main reason is that the platforms ignore the level and Android deprecates announcements, so the suggested wording would be weaker than what the message says now.

The forced `container`: the message says NodeView "put `label` and `description` on a Semantics node around each resolved component, and now maps the other two there", and that `polite`/`assertive` "make that node a live region". Making it a container is the mechanical step that gives the component a node of its own to flag. Without it the Semantics would not be its own node. This is an implementation detail inside the described behaviour, not a design choice that departs from an obvious alternative. The message also says "`off`, or no `live`, sets no flag at all, which leaves the semantics of every other component as it was", which covers the observable effect on components that are not live. Adding a clause about the container is optional polish at most, not something the author's rules require.

Neither part shows a wrong claim or a missing reason under the author's rules, so the finding does not hold even as a nit.

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The problem is real.

**The code.** At 7f5e2045, `argumentErrors` (dart/a2ui_core/lib/src/resolution/data_context.dart, the `checked` map and `_withValidities`) runs every argument through `_withValidities` for every catalog. Nothing checks the protocol version. Both `Catalog.invoke` and rpc_handler.dart:393 call it.

**v0.9 reads such a map differently.** `basicFunctionBodiesV0_9` passes `truthy: isTruthy` (v0_9/functions.dart:31). Only v1.0 passes `isTruthyOrValid` (v1_0/functions.dart:33). The doc comment on `isTruthyOrValid` in function_support.dart, present at this commit, says: "The v0.9 functions keep [isTruthy]: their validation rules return `bool`, and a data-model object that happens to carry a `valid` key is an object." The v0.9 catalog.json types `not.value` as DynamicBoolean. So on v0.9 a `{"valid": false}` map is a schema error, and when it reaches `not` it counts as a truthy object.

**Probe.** I made a throwaway worktree at 7f5e2045 (since removed), with `BasicCatalog.v0_9()` and a v0.9 DataContext:
- At 7f5e2045, `invoke('not', {'value': {'valid': false}})` returned `false`, and `invoke('and', {'values': [{'valid': false}, true]})` returned `true`. Neither raised an error.
- With data_context.dart restored from d7e5f437, both threw `A2uiExpressionError [EXPRESSION_ERROR]: Arguments to 'not'/'and' do not match its schema ... matched 0`.

So on v0.9 the check now reads the operand as `false` and lets it through, while the function reads it as `true`. A schema error that used to be reported becomes a silent wrong result.

**The message is wrong.** It says "because the basic `and`, `or` and `not` read their operands through `ValidationResult.validityOf`". That is true only for the v1.0 basic catalog. Neither the message nor the CHANGELOG mentions any v0.9 effect. The brief counts a wrong claim as a blocker, so blocker severity stands. In practice the behaviour change needs a v0.9 data-model object of exactly the ValidationResult shape bound to a boolean argument, which is an edge case. The false claim alone is enough.

**The proposed fix is right in direction.** `argumentErrors` is an extension on Catalog and has `protocolVersion` in scope. A null version means unversioned, which the catalog doc treats as pre-v1.0. The concrete gate should follow `commonTypesForProtocolVersion`, which already uses `protocolVersion != null && protocolVersion.isAtLeast(A2uiProtocolVersion.v1_0)`.

findings.title: The live-region CHANGELOG line overstates what `live` does
findings.evidence: "A component's `accessibility.live` makes it a live region". `live: "off"` sets no flag, and `assertive` is announced politely, as the message says ("Flutter's `Semantics.liveRegion` is a single flag with no assertive level").
findings.fix: "An `accessibility.live` of `polite` or `assertive` makes a component a live region, announced politely, and ...".

votes.reasoning: I read the brief and commit a465dc4a. In node_view.dart, `live` maps to `true` only for 'polite' or 'assertive'. For 'off' or no value it maps to `null`, and no flag is set. So the CHANGELOG line "A component's `accessibility.live` makes it a live region" is literally untrue for the spec value "off". It also differs from the README sentence in the same commit, which correctly says "an `accessibility.live` of `polite` or `assertive`". Most readers would assume "off" means not live, so the harm is small and this stays a nit. The proposed fix is right in substance. "Announced politely" is optional for a CHANGELOG entry. The README does not mention that downgrade either, so the smallest consistent fix just names the two values, as the README does. No probe was needed because the code and the test settle the behaviour.
votes.corrected_fix: In dart/a2ui_flutter/CHANGELOG.md: "- An `accessibility.live` of `polite` or `assertive` makes a component a live region, and its `accessibility.hidden` excludes it and its subtree from semantics." (Optionally add ", announced politely" after "live region" if the assertive downgrade should be recorded there as well.)

findings.title: The HTML comparison reads two ways, and the nearer reading says something false about HTML
findings.where: message, paragraph 2, lines 1-3: "The player remembers that the current media has been played, so a pause at 0:00, or one before the first position update, keeps the video frame rather than bringing the poster back, as an HTML `<video poster>` does."
findings.evidence: HTML keeps the frame after play then pause at 0:00. The internal play steps (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#internal-play-steps) say: "Change the value of paused to false. If the show poster flag is true, set the element's show poster flag to false and run the time marches on steps." Pausing never sets the flag again. Only the resource selection and load paths do ("Set the element's show poster flag to true", https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#concept-media-load-algorithm). The video element section (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#the-video-element) shows the poster for a paused element only when "the current playback position is the first frame of video, and the element's show poster flag is set". Otherwise it falls to "When the video element is paused: The video element represents the frame of video corresponding to the current playback position." So after play and a pause at 0:00, HTML shows the frame. If "as an HTML `<video poster>` does" attaches to "keeps the video frame", the sentence is true. If it attaches to the nearer phrase "bringing the poster back", it says HTML brings the poster back, which is false. The code matches HTML: `_played = true` is set in the Play handler and `started = ready && (_played || playing || value!.position > Duration.zero)`. This should arguably be a blocker, since the nearest grammatical reading is a wrong claim. It is graded should-fix because the intended meaning is correct.
findings.fix: Replace with: "Like an HTML `<video poster>`, the player does not bring the poster back once the current media has been played, even on a pause at 0:00 or a pause before the first position update."

votes.reasoning:
The intended claim is true, and the code matches it. In the HTML spec, the internal play steps clear the show poster flag. Pausing never sets it again: only the load and resource selection paths do. A paused video with the flag cleared represents the frame at the current position, so HTML keeps the frame after a play and then a pause at 0:00. The 6a244423 diff of media.dart does the same thing. `_played = true` is set in the play handler, `_played = false` is reset when the URL changes, and `started = ready && (_played || playing || value!.position > Duration.zero)` decides whether the poster or the video frame shows. So "keeps the video frame ... as an HTML `<video poster>` does" is accurate, and so is "A new URL starts over".

The ambiguity is real. In "keeps the video frame rather than bringing the poster back, as an HTML `<video poster>` does", the trailing "as ... does" can attach to the nearer "bringing the poster back", and that reading makes a false claim about HTML. The comma before "as" points toward the main clause, which is the correct reading, so most readers will parse it as intended. The finding treats the nearer reading as the more likely one, which I don't accept.

By the author's rules a false claim would be a blocker, but this sentence states a true fact that can be misread. That is a wording problem, so I grade it nit rather than should-fix. The proposed rewrite fixes it. The corrected fix below is a variant that also keeps the "video frame" wording.
votes.corrected_fix: Replace paragraph 2's first sentence with: "Like an HTML `<video poster>`, the player keeps the video frame once the current media has been played, even on a pause at 0:00 or one before the first position update, rather than bringing the poster back." (The reviewer's version is also acceptable.)

votes.reasoning:
The finding is about a wording ambiguity, not a false claim, and I confirm the ambiguity. I read the message and the media.dart diff for commit 6a244423. The code works as the message intends. `_played` resets to false whenever a new URL loads, and the Play handler sets it to true before calling `controller.play()`. `started = ready && (_played || playing || value!.position > Duration.zero)` keeps showing `VideoPlayer` once playback has started, so a pause at 0:00, or a pause before the first position update, does not bring the poster back.

The HTML behaviour the finding cites also checks out. The internal play steps clear the show-poster flag. Pause never sets it again, and only the load and resource-selection algorithms do. So HTML keeps the frame after a play followed by a pause at 0:00, and the message's intended claim is true.

The trailing ", as an HTML `<video poster>` does" comes right after "rather than bringing the poster back". It can fairly be read as "rather than [doing what HTML does,] bringing the poster back", which is the opposite of the facts and of the reason for the choice. I still think most readers attach the clause to the main predicate "keeps the video frame", so this is not a false claim and not a blocker.

The comparison with HTML is the stated reason for the choice. Someone porting the change could misread it as a deliberate departure from HTML, and the fix costs one sentence. That makes it a real but small problem, so I rate it a nit, not the should-fix the reviewer claimed.

The proposed fix is correct but drops the explanation of how it works ("remembers that the current media has been played"). The corrected fix below keeps that explanation and puts the HTML comparison first, where it cannot be misread.
votes.corrected_fix: Replace the first sentence of paragraph 2 with: "Like an HTML `<video poster>`, the player does not bring the poster back once the current media has been played: it remembers the play, so a pause at 0:00, or one before the first position update, keeps the video frame." To avoid a colon, use two sentences: "Like an HTML `<video poster>`, the player does not bring the poster back once the current media has been played. It remembers the play, so a pause at 0:00, or one before the first position update, keeps the video frame."

findings.title: Scrubbing before play diverges from HTML, and the message does not mention it
findings.where: message title and paragraph 1 ("until playback starts"). The behaviour comes from media.dart `started` (`value!.position > Duration.zero`) together with `VideoProgressIndicator(controller, allowScrubbing: true)`.
findings.evidence: In HTML, the first step of the seek algorithm (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-seek) is "Set the media element's show poster flag to false." So any seek before play, even one to 0:00, removes the poster until a new load. In this commit the poster comes from `started`, which is false while `_played` is false, the video is not playing and the position is 0. A scrub away from 0 before play makes `position > 0`, so the poster is dropped. Scrubbing back to the left edge brings the poster back. video_player 2.14.1 `seekTo` clamps to `Duration.zero` and calls `_updatePosition(position)`, so `started` turns false again. HTML does neither. The message says only "until playback starts", which is also wrong for the drop, since a scrub is not playback. It gives no reason for either difference. The likely reason is that `VideoProgressIndicator` exposes no seek callback (its only fields are controller, colors, allowScrubbing and padding), so the player infers a start from the position. The tests at this commit do not exercise scrubbing.
findings.fix: Smallest fix, in the message: add "Scrubbing away from 0:00 also hides the poster. Because the progress bar reports no seeks, the player goes by position, so a scrub back to 0:00 before any play shows the poster again, where HTML keeps the frame after any seek." Also change "until playback starts" in paragraph 1 to "until playback starts or the video moves off 0:00". Alternative, in the code, to match HTML: latch `_played` once `value.position > Duration.zero` is seen, and keep the message as it is.

votes.reasoning:
I read the commit 6a244423 diff, media.dart at that commit, the fake platform, and video_player 2.14.1's `seekTo` and `VideoScrubber`, then ran a probe test in a throwaway worktree (since removed).

At the commit, `started = ready && (_played || playing || value!.position > Duration.zero)`. `_played` is set only by the Play button. `VideoProgressIndicator(controller, allowScrubbing: true)` wraps a `VideoScrubber` whose `onTapDown` and `onHorizontalDragUpdate` call `controller.seekTo` whenever the video is initialized, whether or not it has played. `seekTo` clamps to `[0, duration]` and calls `_updatePosition(position)`, so `value.position` follows the seek directly.

What the probe showed: the Video had a posterUrl, was initialized, and had never been played.
- Tapping the middle of the progress bar gave `seekTo(0, 32)`. The poster Image went away and VideoPlayer was shown (poster=0, player=1).
- Tapping the left edge of the bar gave `seekTo(0, 0)`. The poster came back (poster=1, player=0).
Neither step called `play`.

So both claims in the finding hold:
1. A seek is not playback, yet it removes the poster. That makes the title and paragraph 1 ("until playback starts") wrong for this case.
2. The poster comes back after a seek back to 0:00. That is the reverse of HTML, where the seek algorithm clears the show-poster flag at its first step. Paragraph 2 claims HTML `<video poster>` parity for the pause case and says nothing about seeks.

The message gives no reason for either behaviour. The tests at this commit do not scrub. By the author's rules (every claim true at the commit, reasons given for choices that differ from the obvious one), this is a should-fix. It is not a blocker: the main claim holds for the normal play path, and the gap is a seek-before-play edge case.

The proposed message fix is accurate. I prefer the alternative code fix, though, because it removes a behaviour the message would otherwise have to justify, and it matches the HTML parity paragraph 2 already claims.
votes.corrected_fix:
Preferred, in the code: treat any position past zero as having played. In `_build`, after computing `value`, add `if (ready && value!.position > Duration.zero) _played = true;` and make `started = ready && (_played || playing);`. This is safe to do in build because `_played` only feeds this build and is reset in `_open()`.

Then fix the message to match:
- Title: `feat(a2ui_flutter): show Video.posterUrl until the video plays or seeks`
- Paragraph 1: change "until playback starts" to "until playback starts or the video is scrubbed off 0:00".
- Add this sentence to paragraph 2: "Because the progress bar reports no seeks, a scrub counts as a start once the position moves off 0:00, and the poster then stays hidden, as it does after a seek in HTML."

Add a scrub-before-play test: tap the middle of the bar, expect VideoPlayer, then tap the left edge and still expect VideoPlayer.

If the code stays as it is, the smallest fix is in the message only. Change "until playback starts" in the title and paragraph 1 to "until the video plays or moves off 0:00". Then add: "The progress bar reports no seeks, so the player goes by position. A scrub off 0:00 before playing hides the poster, and a scrub back to 0:00 shows it again, where HTML keeps the video frame after any seek."

votes.reasoning:
I could not refute the behaviour. At 6a244423, media.dart sets `started = ready && (_played || playing || value!.position > Duration.zero)` (L110-111) and shows `VideoPlayer` only when `started || (ready && !hasPoster)` (L128). `_played` is set only by the Play button (L152), and the progress bar is `VideoProgressIndicator(controller, allowScrubbing: true)` (L159). In the pub cache, video_player 2.14.1's `seekTo` clamps a negative position to `Duration.zero` and then calls `_updatePosition(position)` (video_player.dart L842-852). `VideoProgressIndicator`'s only fields are controller, colors, allowScrubbing and padding, so it gives no seek callback. So a scrub before play moves the position above 0 and hides the poster, and a scrub back to 0:00 shows it again. The code at the series head (a465dc4a) is the same, because no later commit touches media.dart. I did not run a widget probe. This is from reading the code.

Why the severity is nit and not should-fix:
(1) The message's HTML claim covers only the pause cases ("a pause at 0:00, or one before the first position update, keeps the video frame ... as an HTML `<video poster>` does"), and that part is accurate. It never claims full HTML parity.
(2) A scrub before play hiding the poster is also what HTML does, because the seek algorithm clears the show-poster flag. So the only real difference from HTML is the corner case where a scrub back to exactly 0:00 brings the poster back. That is cosmetic and harmless.
(3) "until playback starts" in the title and paragraph 1 is loose wording for the scrub case. It echoes the spec's own "before the video plays", and someone porting the code would not be misled about anything that matters.

Still, by the author's rule that every claim must hold at the commit, the summary is not quite exact, and the message leaves the scrub-back difference unexplained. So the finding is real but minor. The proposed message fix is correct but longer than it needs to be, and changing "until playback starts" in the title is not needed.
votes.corrected_fix: Add one sentence to paragraph 2 of the 6a244423 message, after the HTML sentence: "A scrub before play also hides the poster, but because the progress bar reports no seeks, the player goes by position, so a scrub back to 0:00 shows the poster again." Leave the title and paragraph 1 as they are. A code fix that latches `_played` once the position goes above 0 would match HTML exactly. It would need the latch in a controller listener rather than in build, plus a scrub test, which is more than this nit is worth.

findings.title: No reason given for fitting the poster to cover when HTML and Flutter default to contain
findings.where: message paragraph 1: "The media player shows an `http` or `https` poster in the video frame, fitted to cover it, until playback starts." Code: `Image.network(poster, fit: BoxFit.cover, ...)` in media.dart.
findings.evidence: HTML renders the poster the same way as the video, letterboxed. The rendering section (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#embedded-content-rendering-rules) says: "When a video element represents a poster frame or frame of video, the poster frame or frame of video is expected to be rendered at the largest size that maintains the aspect ratio of that poster frame or frame of video without being taller or wider than the video element itself". Its UA stylesheet has `video { object-fit: contain; }`. The Flutter VideoPlayer is also shown uncropped in the AspectRatio box. The v1.0 schema (catalogs/basic/v1/catalog.json L171-L174) says only "The URL of the poster image to display before the video plays." The Video section of basic_catalog_implementation_guide.md (L54-L58) does not mention posters or fit. Nothing in the spec asks for cover, so cover is a choice against the obvious HTML default. Cover crops any poster whose ratio differs from the 16:9 placeholder or from the video's own ratio once it initializes. The message states the choice but gives no reason.
findings.fix: Give the reason, for example: "fitted to cover it rather than letterboxed as HTML does, so the frame shows no empty bars around a poster whose shape differs from the 16:9 placeholder or the video". Or switch to `BoxFit.contain` to match HTML and say so.

votes.reasoning:
I couldn't refute it. At 6a244423, media.dart shows the poster with `Image.network(poster, fit: BoxFit.cover, ...)` inside `AspectRatio(aspectRatio: ready ? value!.aspectRatio : 16 / 9)`. A poster whose ratio differs from 16:9, or from the video's ratio once it initializes, therefore gets cropped.

Nothing in the repository asks for cover:
- The v1.0 schema text, also in typescript/core/web_core/src/catalogs/basic/v1/components/basic_components.ts L192-193, says only "The URL of the poster image to display before the video plays."
- The TypeScript web renderer (web_core Video.ts L37-57) and the Angular renderer (video.component.ts L36) both pass `posterUrl` straight to the native `<video poster>`. Neither sets object-fit on the video. Video.ts styles it `width: 100%; height: auto`, so the browser shows the whole poster: the element either takes the poster's own size or letterboxes it under the UA default `object-fit: contain`. It never crops.

So cover differs from the obvious alternative and from the sibling renderers the brief allows messages to compare with. The brief requires a reason for exactly that kind of choice. The message says "fitted to cover it" with no reason, and the code comments give none either. It is not a wrong claim and it does not break porting, so should-fix rather than blocker.

I checked and found accurate: the message's "fitted to cover it" matches the code, "keeps the 16:9 placeholder ratio until the video reports its own" matches the AspectRatio expression, and the http/https gate on the poster matches `hasPoster`. I did not run a probe, because the claim is about a missing rationale, not about behaviour.
votes.corrected_fix:
The proposed fix holds, with two refinements.

1. To keep cover, name the comparison and the reason, for example: "...in the video frame, fitted to cover it so the frame shows no bars around a poster whose shape differs from the 16:9 placeholder or the video. The web renderers pass the URL to `<video poster>`, which shows the whole poster."

2. To match HTML instead, use `BoxFit.contain` and put the image over the placeholder color, for example `ColoredBox(color: surfaceContainerHighest, child: Image.network(poster, fit: BoxFit.contain, ...))`, so the letterbox bars match the empty frame. Then change the message to "...fitted inside it, letterboxed as HTML `<video poster>` shows it, ...".

votes.reasoning:
I read the brief and `git show 6a244423`. The message says the poster is "fitted to cover it" and the code has `Image.network(poster, fit: BoxFit.cover, ...)` in media.dart, so the message describes the diff accurately. The problem is that it gives no reason for that choice.

The brief requires a reason for each choice, "especially where it differs from the obvious alternative". HTML is the obvious alternative here, and the message itself appeals to HTML: its next paragraph justifies the pause behaviour "as an HTML `<video poster>` does".

HTML letterboxes the poster rather than cropping it:
- The rendering rules say the poster is drawn at the largest size that keeps its aspect ratio inside the element.
- The UA stylesheet has `video { object-fit: contain; }`.

The commit's own `VideoPlayer` path is also uncropped inside the AspectRatio box. So the poster is the one place where the commit departs from both HTML and its own video rendering. A reader expecting HTML parity gets no explanation.

What I checked in the repo:
- The v1 catalog (catalog.json L171-L174) gives only "The URL of the poster image to display before the video plays."
- The Video section of basic_catalog_implementation_guide.md says nothing about posters or fit.
- The blueprint only lists `Video.posterUrl` as an optional v1.0 property.
- No TypeScript renderer in the repo handles posterUrl, so there is no in-repo precedent to cite.

`origin/feat/flutter-adapter-v1_0` also uses `BoxFit.cover`, so the choice causes no porting conflict. It is still unexplained in this message.

There is a plausible reason the message could give. With `contain`, the `Image` has no background inside the AspectRatio, so a mismatched poster would leave transparent bars next to the 16:9 placeholder. Cover fills the frame.

The message makes no false claim, so this is not a blocker. It breaks the author's explicit "reasons for choices" rule at exactly the point where the commit departs from the reference behaviour it cites a few lines later, so it is should-fix rather than a nit.

The proposed fix works. A tighter version is below.
votes.corrected_fix: Replace the second sentence of paragraph 1 with: "The media player shows an `http` or `https` poster in the video frame until playback starts, fitted to cover it so the frame shows no empty bars, where an HTML `<video>` letterboxes a poster whose shape differs from the frame." Alternatively, switch to `BoxFit.contain` behind the placeholder `ColoredBox` (so the bars match the placeholder colour) and say the poster is letterboxed as in HTML.
